Week 6 measured this on assets; today it is measured on your own strategies, where the consequence is that the risk model understates exactly the loss that matters.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report the correlation between your strategies in normal and in stressed periods, separating the conditioning artifact from the real change.
- Say what a risk model built on unconditional correlation understates, and by roughly how much for your book.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Separate artifact from effect as you did on day 41: bucket by combined-book volatility, report strategy correlation per bucket, and run the same bucketing on simulated data with constant true correlation and common volatility. The residual after subtracting the simulated pattern is the real conditional dependence.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Quantify the consequence: compute the book's 99 percent VaR under the unconditional correlation and under the stressed-period correlation. The difference is what your risk model is missing on the days it matters.
:::
:::

::: {.checkpoint}
Your two strategies correlate at 0.1 normally and 0.55 in the worst decile. How much of that is real, and what does it do to your VaR?
